subject: Urgent: Org quota misroute triggered retry storm and 429 flood
messages:
From: Sarah Gomez <sarah.gomez@medicore.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated 429s and timeouts for /generate endpoint (started ~16:45 UTC)

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing a big increase in 429 responses this afternoon for our production org (org-id: MED-772). Approximately 30-60% of calls to /v1/generate return 429, plus a growing number of client timeouts. Our clients implemented aggressive retries and it looks like their retry storms are compounding the problem. This began right after what we think was a quota routing change on Redwood's side at ~16:30 UTC.

Quick notes:
- Sample request ids: req_7b9f, req_7bb3, req_7c0a (logs attached).
- We observed sustained 5xx spikes when upstream started returning 429s.
- This is impacting our real-time feature and causing downstream SLA breaches.

Can someone confirm if any quota/tiering or routing changes were deployed in the last hour? We need immediate mitigation — temporary throttle lift or rollback — and a timeline for resolution.

I've attached a short CSV with error counts and a screenshot of our dashboard.

Thanks,
Sarah Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering
MediCore

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Elevated 429s and timeouts for /generate endpoint (started ~16:45 UTC)

Aisha / team — initial triage: I confirmed a config change deployed at 16:27 UTC as part of a scheduled tiering migration (INFRA rollout). The migration updated label->quota mappings to enforce new per-project caps for a subset of orgs.

Findings:
- MED-772 (MediCore) was incorrectly matched to the "project-tier-beta" policy during label normalization. That policy enforces a conservative per-project token/s rule (approx 12 rps effective) — far below their normal rate.
- Traffic from multiple projects under MED-772 was funneled through a single project-level quota because of a label collision in the normalization logic. The effective limit was reached quickly and returned 429s.
- Customer-side client retries (exponential backoff misconfigured) amplified the surge into a retry storm, causing additional backend pressure and intermittent 5xx timeouts.

Immediate remediation applied (16:45–17:05 UTC):
1) Rolled back the tiering migration for the affected mapping (routing-config-diff.txt attached).
2) Temporarily increased project-level quota for MED-772 to match their committed baseline throughput.
3) Added an emergency alert rule to stop aggressive retries from downstream proxies (rate limit amplification detection).

Current status (17:28): 429 rate has dropped from ~48% to ~6% for MED-772; error rate trending down. Continued monitoring for the next 3 hours.

Next steps:
- Permanent fix: update label normalization to prefer explicit project tags over inferred labels (patch queued: INFRA-PR-1456).
- Postmortem: capture root cause (label collision + conservative fallback policy) and update rollout checklist to include canary verification of per-project mappings.
- Customer remediation: propose service credit for the incident window; sales to handle.

I'll hold open a hotline if we need to reapply measures.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
